pull_requests.title: fix: publish PR updates resumably and give retries their own limit
pull_requests.author: jtbinith
pull_requests.description:
Closes #59

**PRD ID:** Q4 (factory) · **Threat IDs:** none (no change to `web/`)

## Why
At 09:51 on PR #52 the runner pushed round 1's fix (`708c84b`), then `gh pr edit` hit this repo's classic-projects error, the same `gh` bug the skill already avoids. The red → green proof was never posted. A review of the whole runner then found:
1. `gh pr edit` fails here, and `gh pr comment` is untried.
2. Publishing isn't resumable: the push is recorded first, so after a crash a retry just waits and the proof is never posted.
3. Three `/agent retry` comments, all spent on runner bugs, used up the 3 rounds meant for instructions. The next retry would have been refused.
4. The after-run GitHub check read only the first 100 issue events. #41 is getting close.

## What changes
- **Resumable publishing:** the runner counts which proofs are on the PR. Every step (push, retry, reopen) first posts anything pushed but not yet posted: the description through `gh api -X PATCH`, and each proof as an issue comment on the PR (the same call as ticket comments, already proven).
- **Retries have their own limit (5)**, separate from instructions (3), since a retry starts no agent.
- **Every page** of comments and events is read (`allPages`).
- **`QODO_DRY_RUN=1`** (with `QODO_STATE` for a copy of the state): every GitHub write and push is logged instead of done, and it stops before any agent run or wait. The runner can be rehearsed.
- Qodo's review time is measured from its own comment, not from when the runner looked.

## Commits
| Commit | | Unit tests |
|---|---|---|
| `5cc1088` test | unposted proofs (including a run saved before tracking), every page, a separate retry limit | red: 3 of 17 fail (AssertionErrors) |
| `53fca26` fix | resumable publishing, `gh api`, pages, retry limit, dry run | 17/17 |
| `7b97bed`, `829263e` fix | review timing from the push and from Qodo's comment | |
| `0675105` test (Qodo on 829263e) | publish from what's on the PR; over-limit comments marked read | red: 2 of 18 fail |
| fix (head) | `publishPlan`, `askPlan`, dry run only on a copy, no git steps in a dry pick-up | 18/18 |

## Qodo's review of 829263e
| # | Finding | Verdict | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dry runs can discard pending PR proofs | Real (dry run on live state) | A dry run refuses to start without `QODO_STATE` |
| 2 | A rehearsal can replace a real worktree | Real | A dry pick-up stops before any git or worktree step |
| 3 | Older PRs receive duplicate proofs | Real in general | What to publish is read from the PR itself (its description and the runner's comments), not from a count |
| 4 | Interrupted publishing repeats comments | Real | Same change: already-posted proofs are found on the PR |
| 5 | Queued retries evade their limit | **Not changed.** The limits count rounds of work, not comments: retries queued in one poll do one re-check, and a retry sent with an instruction is covered by that round's checks | — |
| 6 | An extra retry repeatedly stops the run | Real | A batch of comments is marked read before any limit check (`askPlan` always consumes) |

## Tested
- `npm run test:unit` in the runner's container: 55/55.
- `QODO_DRY_RUN=1` without `QODO_STATE`: refused, exit 2.
- `gh api -X PATCH …/pulls/52` with #52's own description: works. (The first try added a trailing newline. It was restored byte-identical.)
- **Dry run of the real next step**, `/agent retry` on #52, against a copy of #41's state, with nothing written:
```
DRY RUN would update PR #52's description
DRY RUN would comment on #52: **Red → green, checked by the runner** (not the agent) for 943d63f..708c84b:
#41 published on PR #52: description and 1 proof comment
#41 owner retry: nothing new to push, waiting for Qodo's review of 708c84b again
#41 Qodo reviewed 708c84b 93 s after the push: no open findings
DRY RUN would label #41: +agent-done, +needs-manual-check
```

(In a dry run nothing is really posted, so the next step plans the same post again. In a real run it then finds the proof on the PR and posts nothing.)

pull_requests.title: fix: let the unattended agent run its test commands
pull_requests.author: jtbinith
pull_requests.description:
Closes #55

**PRD ID:** Q4 (factory) · **Threat IDs:** none (no change to `web/`)

## Why
On #41 the unattended agent couldn't run a single test, twice. Every command "required approval" nobody could give, so it said so, claimed no pass and left the runner's own `npm test` as the only result. Probing the runner's settings one rule at a time showed why: a prefix rule only matches when a space follows the prefix. `Bash(npm run test:*)` never matched `npm run test:unit`, and `Bash(node tests/:*)` never matched `node tests/two-browser.mjs`. Pipes and `2>&1` add parts that need their own approval.

## What changes
- The test commands that take no arguments are allowed exactly: `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:browsers`, `node tests/two-browser.mjs` and `node tests/two-browser.mjs --relay`. `npm test …` and `node --test …` stay prefix rules (they match).
- The skill lists those commands and says to add nothing: no `2>&1`, pipes or `cd … &&`.

## Tested
The agent was asked to run each command once, with the runner's real ALLOW and DENY lists read from this branch's `scripts/agent-watch.mjs`, its settings and its container (from `test-permission-probe.log`):
```
npm run test:unit                    -> allowed, ran ["npm run test:unit"] | All 50 unit tests passed and none failed.
node --test tests/thumb.test.mjs     -> allowed, ran ["node --test tests/thumb.test.mjs"] | All 5 tests in `tests/thumb.test.mjs` passed, with none failing, cancelled or skipped.
node tests/two-browser.mjs --relay   -> allowed, ran ["node tests/two-browser.mjs --relay"] | All 28 checks in the relay run passed, and none failed.
```
Before the fix, the same probe denied `npm run test:unit` under `Bash(npm run test:*)`.

No unit test: the behaviour lives in Claude Code's permission matching, so the probe above is the check.

pull_requests.author: jtbinith
pull_requests.description:
Closes #54

**PRD ID:** Q4 (factory) · **Threat IDs:** none (no change to `web/`)

> **History replaced.** Rebuilt from `416e751` into refactor → test → fix commits, so red can be checked from the history. Qodo's review of `416e751` (4 findings) is in this PR's timeline. Its fixes are in the commits marked "Qodo on 416e751" below.

## Why
From #41's run on PR #52.
- **Round 1 stopped on a runner bug.** The agent's new test `756e022` really failed on its own (`FAIL tapping while every incoming slot is taken says "Receiving…" and asks for nothing`), but its `check(…)` call wraps across two lines. The runner read test names one line at a time, found none and refused the proof. That failed safe but was wrong.
- **There was no way to say "the runner was wrong, check again"** without starting a whole new run.
- **The agent's first run couldn't run any tests:** only `npm test` exactly was allowed, so `npm test 2>&1 | tail` needed approval nobody could give. It said so and claimed no pass.
- Qodo's finding titles reached the log escaped (`isn't`).

## Commits (each red fails on assertions only, never an import error: the tests import the module as a namespace)
| Commit | What | Unit tests |
|---|---|---|
| `ad739f7` refactor | the helpers move to `scripts/runner-lib.mjs`, unchanged | |
| `9e71fb7` test | wrapped `check()` names (the #41 case), decoding, `/agent retry` | red: 3 of 8 fail |
| `7fead18` fix | read each `check()` call to its closing bracket | 8/8 |
| `377ea42` test (Qodo on 416e751, findings 3 and 4, plus a comment case) | regex literals, comments, other hunks | red: 3 of 11 fail |
| `64fa751` fix | skip regex literals and comments, one hunk at a time | 11/11 |
| `61e6870` test (Qodo on 416e751, finding 1) | a retry with nothing new waits for Qodo | red: 1 of 12 fails |
| `22477f8` fix | `/agent retry`, reopen stopped runs, `npm test` with arguments, decoded titles | 12/12 |
| `900aaf1` test (Qodo on 22477f8, finding 2) | a retry sent with an instruction when the agent commits nothing | red: 1 of 13 fails |
| `0191b36` fix | apply that retry as if it came alone | 13/13 |
| `608b6a8` test (Qodo on 0191b36) | an instruction the agent makes no change for stops and asks you, retry or not | red: 1 of 13 fails |
| `7bffb42` fix | stop with `agent-needs-help` instead of waiting (replaces `0191b36`'s rule) | 13/13 |

## Qodo's review of 416e751
| # | Finding | Verdict | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Retry after a push skips every check | Real | `61e6870` → `22477f8`: with nothing new, a retry waits for Qodo again |
| 2 | Mixed requests silently lose retry checks | **Not lost, final answer.** When the agent commits something, the checks, push and Qodo wait that follow cover the retry. When it commits nothing, `0191b36` first applied the retry as a wait, but Qodo then showed (below) that this could mark the run done with your request undone. So the run now **stops and asks you**, saying a lone `/agent retry` re-runs the checks. Nothing is lost silently | `900aaf1` → `0191b36`, then `608b6a8` → `7bffb42` |
| new on `0191b36` | Owner requests can be marked done unfixed | **Real** | `608b6a8` → `7bffb42` |
| 3 | Regex conditions hide failing new tests | Real | `377ea42` → `64fa751` |
| 4 | Unrelated edits can certify a red test | Real | `377ea42` → `64fa751` |

`/agent retry` counts towards the 3 comment rounds, and the runner's comment says so.

## Tested
- `testNames` on `756e022`'s real diff finds its name, and the real red output then counts as an assertion failure. `d09c9bf` (accepted in round 0) still gives the same 5 names.
- `npm run test:unit` in the runner's container: 50/50 (37 + 13 new).

## After merge
`systemctl --user daemon-reload` (the timer's service file changed), then `/agent retry` on PR #52.

**PRD ID:** Q4 (factory) · **Threat IDs:** none (no change to `web/`)

Changes from the first unattended runs (#19, #41, #49 on 13 Nov).

pull_requests.title: chore: run ready-for-agent tickets without a session
pull_requests.author: jtbinith
pull_requests.description:
Closes nothing (factory change). **PRD ID:** Q4 · **Threat IDs:** none (no change to `web/`)

## What this adds
A ticket labelled `ready-for-agent` is worked without anyone opening a session.

- `scripts/agent-watch.mjs`, one step per run:
  1. **Pick up** an open issue written by jtbinith and labelled `ready-for-agent` by jtbinith (checked from the issue's events). Refuse it if anything in its blocked-by list is open.
  2. A Claude Code subagent works it with the work-ticket skill, in its own worktree on `agent/<N>-…`.
  3. **The runner checks, not the agent:** what changed on GitHub during the run (refs, the owner's comments and events), guarded paths, the exit code. Then `npm test`. Then every `test:` commit must touch only `tests/` and fail on its own **on one of the tests it adds**. Then it pushes and opens the PR with that red → green proof.
  4. **Review loop:** once Qodo has reviewed the exact pushed commit, its open findings, or a `/agent …` comment from jtbinith, go to a new subagent run. Then step 3 again.
  5. `agent-done` when Qodo has no open findings. `agent-needs-help` when a limit is hit, the agent stops, a check fails or the runner crashes.
- `scripts/systemd/`: a user timer runs the copy on origin/main every 10 minutes. Once a ticket is picked up, the run stays until it's done or stopped, waiting for Qodo itself.
- Work-ticket skill: an **Unattended runs** section. The agent reads the ticket and review from `.agent/`, writes its PR body, report and **Assumptions** there, and stops by writing `.agent/stop.md`.
- AGENTS.md: Layout row and setup steps.

## Limits and why
| Limit | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Check for the label | every 10 min | Pick-up delay doesn't matter much. Calm when nothing is labelled |
| Look for Qodo's review mid-run | every 30 s | Re-reviews were measured at about 1 min, so a round doesn't sit idle |
| Wait for Qodo after a push | 10 min | Measured on PRs #39–#47: first review 0:25–3:19, re-review about 1 min. 10 min is about 3× the slowest |
| `npm test` attempts per round | 2 | The second agent run gets the failing lines |
| Qodo review rounds | 3 | Then `agent-needs-help` |
| `/agent` comment rounds | 3 | Then `agent-needs-help` |
| One agent run | 45 min | |

## Trust
- The agent runs with no user settings, no MCP servers and no `gh`. It gets only file tools, the tests and local git (`git push`, `checkout`, `switch`, `reset`, `remote`, `gh`, `curl`, `wget` and web access are denied). It reads GitHub only through files the runner writes, holding text from jtbinith and qodo-code-review only.
- Code the agent writes runs only in a throwaway container (`mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.64.1-noble`): the agent's `node`/`npm` and all of the runner's tests go through it. It sees the worktree and `node_modules`, not the home directory, so no gh login, SSH keys, AWS or Claude settings. No published ports. Checked: `.ssh`, `.config/gh`, `.aws` and `Documents` are hidden and a GitHub API call from inside gets 401.
- The tool list blocks GitHub access, edits are limited to the worktree, file reads of secret folders are denied, and the runner checks after every run (GitHub footprint, guarded paths, uncommitted changes, exit code).
- Red must be an **AssertionError** in a test the `test:` commit adds, not a crash. Checked on #27's `d32e681` (accepted) and the same test with a ReferenceError (rejected).
- The runner pushes only `agent/*` branches. main is protected by a ruleset (PR required, no force pushes, no deletion). Nothing merges itself.

## Tested
- Dry run with nothing labelled: exits 0, lock released.
- The isolated agent lists only Bash, Edit, Glob, Grep, Read, Skill and Write, with no MCP tools, and the work-ticket skill is available.
- Qodo review parsing: PR #40's first review → 6 open findings at `a05845c` (the commit pushed). The final reviews of #40, #44 and #47 → 0 open.

pull_requests.title: docs: plan join tabs, group sharing and device identity
pull_requests.author: jtbinith
pull_requests.description:
Docs only. No code changes. Plans the next round of joining, sharing and identity work. It also writes down the later reliability design so earlier changes don't block it.

**PRD IDs:** C2 (withdrawn), C3, C15, C16, F10–F18, N4, S2, S3, S18–S20, R1–R5, OQ9, OQ10 · **Threat IDs:** T-S6, T-S7, T-S8, T-T5, T-R1, T-I12, T-D10, MUC9, MUC10

## What changes
- **Joining screens (PRD UC2, C15, C16):** orbs are withdrawn (C2). Screens join by tapping join tabs on facing edges or with a mini-map where each person moves only their own tile and the other device must accept. Both have Undo or "No".
- **Sharing in a group (F11–F15, UC9):** joined screens receive by themselves up to 20 MB, "Share with everyone" with a tray, "Save all" and later receipts and catch-up for late arrivals.
- **Dragging (F16–F18):** a print can't get stuck at a screen's edge or on a shared edge, click to pick up and drop on laptops and drags stay clear of the phone's own gestures.
- **Identity (S2, S18–S20):** a reload is the same device coming back, names are unique per room by a name key (case, full-width letters, accents, invisible characters and mixed scripts), remembered devices are off by default and each device has a colour and icon from its key. The four words (S3) become an optional "Check this device" step.
- **Later (PRD 7.6, ARCHITECTURE 13):** piece hashes, any holder sends any piece, spreading through the room, chaos tests and a dashboard, repair pieces.
- **Threat model and test plan:** new threats, misuse cases MUC9 and MUC10 plus a test row for every new requirement.

## Notes
- S2 follows #24's design: the device id is the hash of its public key. Only room messages and passed-on data get an extra ECDSA signature.
- Keys can't go in `sessionStorage` (it only stores text), so S18 keeps a tab id there and the keys in IndexedDB.
- `AGENTS.md` still says "push orbs". It changes with the code when C15 ships, not in this PR.
- ARCHITECTURE 13 lists two bugs in today's code: missing pieces are only asked from the first sender. Pieces already received are thrown away when a link falls back to the relay. They get their own ticket.
- Tickets for these requirements are filed after this merges.

pull_requests.title: S14: don't decode thumbnails over 400 x 400
pull_requests.author: jtbinith
pull_requests.description:
Closes #27

**PRD ID:** S14 · **Threat IDs:** T-D8 (closed), T-E3 (narrowed, still open), MUC5

## Acceptance
- [x] A thumbnail over 400 × 400 isn't decoded. `thumbFits` in `web/check.js` reads the JPEG frame header without decoding; `done()` in `web/index.html` only keeps and decodes a thumbnail it accepts. Two-browser test: B's `createImageBitmap` is never called for the 401 × 400 thumbnail or the 30000 × 30000 bomb (direct and relay).
- [x] The print shows a plain card. Rejected thumbnails leave `p.img` and `p.thumb` null, so the print draws as the card and the thumbnail isn't passed on to late guests.

## Edge case
- Exactly 400 × 400 is decoded and shown at 400 × 400. 401 × 400 and 400 × 401 are not.
- Also not decoded: height given later (DNL, height 0), zero width, a small frame then a huge second frame, lossless/arithmetic/hierarchical frames (we never send them), PNG and other formats, cut-off files, empty or missing bytes.

## Red (before the fix)
Test commit 0ef022a with `thumbFits` stubbed to always return true:
```
✖ a thumbnail over 400 x 400 is not decoded        AssertionError: 401 x 400  true !== false
✖ a thumbnail whose size can't be read is not decoded  AssertionError: height given later (DNL)  true !== false
ℹ tests 36  ℹ pass 34  ℹ fail 2
FAIL a 401 x 400 thumbnail isn't decoded and the print shows a plain card ({"img":[401,400],"kept":true,"decoded":true})
FAIL a 30000 x 30000 bomb thumbnail isn't decoded and the print shows a plain card ({"img":null,"kept":true,"decoded":true})
```
(both browser lines failed in the direct run and the relay run)

## Tested
`npm test` on 0c8c659: unit 36/36 pass. Two-browser direct: every check PASS, including
```
PASS a 400 x 400 thumbnail is shown ({"img":[400,400],"kept":true,"decoded":true})
PASS a 401 x 400 thumbnail isn't decoded and the print shows a plain card ({"img":null,"kept":false,"decoded":false})
PASS a 30000 x 30000 bomb thumbnail isn't decoded and the print shows a plain card ({"img":null,"kept":false,"decoded":false})
```
Relay (`went relay (encrypted)`): every check PASS, same three lines.

## Notes
- New unit file `tests/thumb.test.mjs`, added to `test:unit` in `package.json`. Fixture helpers `sizedJpeg`, `twoFrameJpeg` and `smallPng` in `tests/jpeg-fixtures.mjs`.
- The limit is a named constant: `LIMITS.thumbSide = 400`.
- T-E3 (exploit the image decoder) still lists S14 as planned: small thumbnails are still decoded, so this narrows that threat but doesn't close it.
- Docs: THREAT-MODEL T-D8 moved to In place; ARCHITECTURE `chunk` row names `thumbFits`; TESTING S14 marked (exists).

## After review
Qodo found 0 issues. A separate review found one gap: `thumbFits` stopped at the first end marker and ignored anything after it. Ultra HDR keeps a gain map there, so a 400 × 400 first image could carry a huge second image past the check (the same trailing data #26 strips when sending). Fixed test first:
- `d32e681` test (red: unit 36/37 on the assertion "400 x 400 followed by 30000 zero bytes"; the browser check FAILed because Chrome decoded it)
- `2271aa5` fix: the end marker must be the last two bytes. Green: unit 37/37, direct and relay PASS. Our own thumbnails end at the marker.

## After the rules
- Tests were committed on their own before the fix, and red was an assertion failure.
- Rule 3: the limit is a named constant, and a rejected thumbnail is neither kept nor counted as done.
- Qodo findings: #26 7, #18 4, #27 0. #27 is also the smallest of the three, so this shows fewer findings after the rules, not that the rules caused it.

pull_requests.title: fix: give up on a send after 10 s with no progress
pull_requests.author: jtbinith
pull_requests.description:
Closes #18

**PRD ID:** S1.3 (sender error via toast, ahead of F2) · **Threat IDs:** T-D4

## Acceptance
- [x] A send gives up after 10 s with no progress (named constants): `SEND_TIMEOUT = 10000` and `DRAIN_CHECK = 1000` in `web/peers.js`. Unit: still pending at 9.999 s, rejected at 10 s, for both a missing key (relay) and a buffer that never drains (direct). Two-browser: gave up after 10.0 s, direct and relay.
- [x] The timer restarts whenever the key arrives or the buffer drains. Unit: a key at 9 s lets the send finish. Two pieces that each wait 9 s on a full buffer both go through (18 s total). Once the key arrives the frame joins the shared relay queue and its timer stops, because that queue is pacing and not a wait on the device.
- [x] The send is cancelled: `sendFile` rejects with `SendTimeout` and sends nothing more. Unit: a piece that timed out is not sent when the key turns up later.
- [x] The sender sees an error: a toast says "Couldn’t send photo-1.jpg to <device>: it stopped answering". Two-browser checks the toast on the sending page. This is a toast for now, not the full F2 progress UI (#30).
- [x] The receiver can ask again. Unit: after the timeout a new request to the same device goes through once its key arrives. Nothing is left that blocks a retry. The receiver's existing resend loop (C12) still asks every few seconds.

## Edge case
- A silent third device times out while two others keep transferring. Unit: a send to `b` finishes while the send to `c` is still waiting. Then `c` gives up at 10 s. Later sends to `b` still work. Two-browser: a device that never answers asks A for photo-1.jpg. A drags photo-1.jpg to B, which gets it in 0.2 s (direct) or 0.4 s (relay). A gives up on the silent device after 10.0 s.
- A throttled but working link finishes. Unit: the buffer drains 50 KB a second for 25 s without reaching the low mark. The send never gives up. It finishes when the buffer drains. The two-browser test can't throttle a real link. This is checked by the unit test only.
- A short message (`send`) to a silent device is dropped quietly after 10 s instead of becoming an unhandled rejection.

## Red (before the fix)
Commit `1130992` (tests only):
```
✖ a send to a device that never sends its key gives up after 10 s
  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: still waiting after 10 s
    actual: 'pending', expected: 'rejected'
✖ the cancelled send is not delivered late, and the receiver can ask again
    actual: 'pending', expected: 'rejected'
✔ a key that arrives before 10 s lets the send finish
✖ a direct link whose buffer never drains gives up after 10 s
  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: still waiting after 10 s
    actual: 'pending', expected: 'rejected'
✔ the timer restarts whenever the buffer drains
✔ a throttled but working link finishes
✖ a silent device times out while two others keep transferring
    actual: 'pending', expected: 'rejected'
✖ a short message to a silent device is dropped after 10 s without an error
    actual: 'pending', expected: 'fulfilled'
ℹ tests 8  ℹ pass 3  ℹ fail 5
```
Two-browser (direct):
```
PASS photo-1.jpg reached B after 0.2 s, while A still waited on the silent device
FAIL send to a silent device gave up and told the sender (after 20.2 s)
```
The three tests that passed already guard the edge cases (a working or throttled link must not be cut off).

## Review fixes
Qodo found 2 bugs. Both were confirmed and fixed. Each fix has a `test:` commit (red) then a `fix:` commit:

| Finding | Red | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Slow peers never see shared photos. A print dropped after the timeout was still counted as sent. A regression this PR caused | `✖ a short message says whether it was sent or dropped. AssertionError: a dropped message was reported as sent` | `send` reports whether it was sent. A dropped print is un-counted and announced again when the device's key arrives |
| File errors blame the other device | `FAIL a read error isn't blamed on the other device ("…: it stopped answering")` | Only a timeout says the other device stopped answering |
| **Found next to the change:** one relay frame that throws breaks the relay queue for every device (it was already there before this PR) | `✖ one relay frame that fails to send doesn't block later frames. AssertionError: a later frame to another device never went out` | Each frame fails on its own. The queue carries on |

Qodo's re-review found 2 more, both in that new test, not the product code. Both were confirmed and fixed in `test:` commits (no red, as they are test changes):
- **Direct checks fail on working links:** a direct link opening during the hold could deliver the print early. The scenario now runs relay-only.
- **Fast re-announcements fail the check:** "B doesn't have it yet" was read after the key was released. It's now recorded in the page at the moment of release.

Also found while re-running: the unit test for the relay queue was flaky (and could hang). It moved the mocked clock before real WebCrypto had sealed the frame. It now waits for the frame first. 30 of 30 runs pass on their own. 10 of 10 full unit runs pass. `waitFor` is bounded by real time (2 s) rather than loop turns. Slow WebCrypto on CI won't fail it falsely. The test still fails with the old `enqueue`. Put back for one uncommitted run, it failed on `AssertionError: a later frame to another device never went out`.

The re-announce path now has a two-browser check as well: B's key is held back for 11 s. A's print to B is dropped. Then B gets it once the key arrives. It passed straight away. It's a regression guard. With the fix taken out, it fails (checked once).

## Tested
`npm test` after the fixes:
```
ℹ pass 32
ℹ fail 0
PASS photo-1.jpg reached B after 0.3 s, while A still waited on the silent device
PASS send to a silent device gave up and told the sender (after 10.0 s)
PASS a read error isn't blamed on the other device ("Couldn’t send photo-1.jpg to a device")
PASS A dropped its print to B while B's key was late
PASS A announced the print again once B's key came, and B has it (0.0 s direct, 0.1 s relay after the key)
```
Direct and relay: every check PASS. exit 0.

## Notes
- `window.__t` now exposes `onMessage` so the two-browser test can send a `want` from a device that never answers. It is a test hook, like `expect` and `dropped`.
- A bad key still drops held frames and resolves the send without telling anyone (unchanged).
- Docs: THREAT-MODEL T-D4 moves S1.3 from Planned to In place. TESTING.md has a new S1.3 row (exists). ARCHITECTURE.md is unchanged: no message, key or check changed.
- Not checked on real devices (needs the user): a phone that locks its screen mid-send.
- The ticket was incomplete: "the receiver can ask again" holds for files, not prints. See the comment on #18.

pull_requests.title: feat: remove location and camera details from JPEG photos
pull_requests.author: jtbinith
pull_requests.description:
Closes #26

**PRD ID:** S6 (US5) · **Threat IDs:** T-I5, MUC4

## Acceptance
- [x] A JPEG with GPS, including an iPhone fixture, arrives with none: `IMG_0001.JPG` (iPhone-style: EXIF with GPS + Apple maker note, XMP, ICC, MPF, HDR gain map after the main image) arrives on B with no GPS, Make, Model or gain map. Direct and relay: PASS.
- [x] Still upright: Orientation 6 is kept. B decodes it as 8 x 16 (the stored image is 16 x 8). Direct and relay: PASS.
- [x] "Keep details" sends the original: `IMG_0003.JPG` sent with the box ticked arrives byte-identical with GPS still there. Direct and relay: PASS.
- [x] Real iPhone: two photos picked on an iPhone (`IMG_7750`, `IMG_7748`) came out of the picker as JPEGs that still carried GPS, camera details and the gain map. `stripJpeg` removed all three and kept the orientation. Recorded in PRD S17 and threat T-I5.
- [x] Passes its fingerprint check: the SHA-256 is taken of the cleaned file. B kept it with the announced SHA. Direct and relay: PASS.
- [x] Colour profile kept: the ICC_PROFILE segment comes through unchanged (unit).

## Edge case
- A JPEG without metadata is unchanged: plain and progressive fixtures come out byte-identical (unit). Chrome's canvas JPEG `photo-0.jpg` still arrives byte-identical (two-browser). PASS.
- A HEIC is sent with a "details not removed" warning: the toast says `5 on the table. Details not removed from IMG_0002.HEIC` and B gets the print. PASS.
- A JPEG that can't be read to the end is sent unchanged with the same warning. It isn't guessed at (unit). PASS.
- Every other file the picker accepts (video, PNG, WebP, HEIC) is sent with the warning: `5 on the table. Details not removed from clip.mp4, IMG_0002.HEIC`. PASS.

## Red (before the fix)
`web/strip.js` was a stub that removed nothing (checkbox and `prepareFile` call already wired in).

Unit (`node --test tests/strip.test.mjs`): 4 pass, 7 fail, for example:
```
✖ an iPhone JPEG loses GPS, camera details, XMP, MPF and the gain map but stays upright
  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: no GPS
  + { latitude: 51.50055555555556, longitude: -0.12444444444444444 }
  - undefined
✖ an Android JPEG (little-endian EXIF, IPTC, comment, progressive) loses its details
  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: no GPS
✖ a JPEG with GPS but no rotation gets no EXIF at all
✖ a broken JPEG is not guessed at
✖ file types are recognised from their contents
✖ edge: a HEIC is sent unchanged with a "details not removed" warning
✖ a JPEG that can't be read is sent with the same warning
```
Two-browser (direct):
```
FAIL HEIC warned: "5 on the table"
FAIL IMG_0001.JPG arrived without GPS, camera details or gain map
exit 1
```

## Review fixes
Qodo found 4 bugs and 2 requirement gaps. Its re-review found 1 more bug. All seven were confirmed. Each fix has its own `test:` commit (red) followed by its `fix:` commit (green):

| Finding | Red | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| APP0 and Adobe segments copied whole | `✖ JFIF and Adobe segments keep only their fixed fields — AssertionError: no extra bytes` | Keep only their fixed fields. The JFIF thumbnail is dropped |
| Videos, PNG and WebP sent with no warning | `FAIL video and HEIC warned: "5 on the table. Details not removed from IMG_0002.HEIC"` | Warn for every file that isn't a cleaned JPEG |
| TEM marker read as having a length | `✖ a TEM marker … AssertionError: stripped, not given up on` | Read TEM as a 2-byte marker |
| A JPEG labelled as HEIC is never cleaned | `✖ a JPEG named or typed as HEIC is still cleaned` | Check the bytes before the type |
| No "Keep details" option | (requirement gap) | Restored in `feat: restore Keep details (canary over)`. It was removed on purpose before review to test whether Qodo compares the PR with the ticket. It did |
| The real-iPhone GPS result isn't recorded | (requirement gap) | Checked on a real iPhone. See Acceptance |
| Batch photos can leak GPS after a toggle (found on re-review) | `FAIL IMG_0005.JPG cleaned though "Keep details" was ticked mid-batch` | Read Keep details once per pick |

## Tested
`npm test` after the fixes:
```
ℹ pass 21
ℹ fail 0
-- direct --
PASS video and HEIC warned: "5 on the table. Details not removed from clip.mp4, IMG_0002.HEIC"
PASS IMG_0001.JPG passed its fingerprint check
PASS IMG_0001.JPG arrived without GPS, camera details or gain map
PASS IMG_0001.JPG still upright (shown 8 x 16)
PASS IMG_0003.JPG ("Keep details") still has its GPS
PASS IMG_0004.JPG cleaned though "Keep details" was ticked mid-batch
PASS IMG_0005.JPG cleaned though "Keep details" was ticked mid-batch
PASS IMG_0006.JPG kept its details though "Keep details" was unticked mid-batch
PASS IMG_0007.JPG kept its details though "Keep details" was unticked mid-batch
PASS went direct
-- relay --
(the same checks, all PASS, with "went relay (encrypted)")
exit 0
```

## Notes
- The iPhone fixture is synthetic. It is built in `tests/jpeg-fixtures.mjs` and copies an iPhone photo's layout around a real 16 x 8 JPEG. It has not been compared with a photo from a real iPhone. No real photo or location is committed: the GPS is Big Ben.
- The two-browser drag helper now brings the print to the top before pressing. Overlapping prints can't make it pick up the wrong one (there are 5 prints now).
- JPEGs are read into memory whole to be cleaned. That is local work on the sender only, capped by C14's 200 MB.
- Design choice: a JPEG that can't be read to the end is sent as the original with a "details not removed" warning, not refused. The sender is told. Refusing would be stricter.
- AGENTS.md: added `web/strip.js` to the Layout table.
- The setting is fixed when the files are picked. Changing it mid-batch applies to the next pick. Both directions are tested (ticked and unticked mid-batch).

pull_requests.author: jtbinith
pull_requests.description:
Day 2: the factory's house rules.

**AGENTS.md** gives coding agents and reviewers what they need: what the app is, the file layout, setup and verify commands, five rules and known gaps.

Rules, each with where it applies, why it exists and how it's checked:
- **Security and privacy:** 1. nothing from another device is used until `check.js` accepts it · 2. the room server only ever sees sealed bytes
- **Network reliability:** 3. no device can hold up anyone else · 4. a file is kept only if it matches its fingerprint
- **Verification:** 5. joining and transfer changes pass the two-browser test before merging

**Runnable checks** (`npm test`):
- `tests/check.test.mjs`: unit tests for `web/check.js`
- `tests/two-browser.mjs`: two browser windows join a room, join screens, share and drag photos. Checks files arrive byte-identical, malformed messages are ignored and a late guest still sees held photos. Runs direct and with the encrypted relay forced.
- `tests/serve.mjs`: serves `web/` on 127.0.0.1 only

**Tested:** `npm test` passes: 6 unit tests, 14 two-browser checks (7 direct, 7 relay).

pull_requests.title: Start universal sharing, replacing Polywogs
pull_requests.author: jtbinith
pull_requests.description:
I changed my mind about the project, so this replaces the Polywogs code with universal sharing (name to come): like AirDrop, but for every device and a whole group at once.

**What it does**
- Devices join a room with a code, and pushing orbs to a shared edge joins their screens into one shared space.
- Photos and videos appear as prints everyone can see. Dragging a print onto your screen brings the full original file to your device; tap to save.
- Files go directly device to device over WebRTC. When the network blocks that (hotel Wi-Fi, mobile data), they go through the Supabase room end-to-end encrypted (ECDH P-256 + HKDF + AES-256-GCM, see `web/seal.js`).
- Pages now publishes `web/` as a static site.

**Tested**
- iPhone 12 (Safari, iOS 26) and a Linux laptop on hotel Wi-Fi: photos both ways, through the encrypted relay.
- Local two-browser test: photo and video arrive byte-identical over both paths.

**Known gaps** (listed in the README): the server could swap public keys, anyone with the room code can join, iPhone saves videos as files, the relay is slow.

The Polywogs history and pull requests stay in this repo.

pull_requests.title: Day 1 (part 2): every polywog gets a job, stats and a trump card
pull_requests.author: jtbinith
pull_requests.description:
## What this does

After a Tinkercad model wakes up on the island, it works out what kind of polywog it is.

1. A thought bubble pops up and a glowing ring scans down its body.
2. Its job icon pops up in a speech bubble (icons only, no words): courier, keeper, fan or bridge.
3. A trump card slides in with its picture, a name the kid can change, its job, three stats and what the job does, plus **Change job** and **Export for Tinkercad**. It tucks into a stack after a few seconds; tap to open it again.
4. Then it sets off, moving in a way that matches its stats. Polywogs bump into each other instead of walking through.

## How the job and stats are worked out

- `web/look/roles.ts` measures the model (how long, how flat, how solid, how pointy) and scores each job with weights. The best score wins.
- Close calls are nudged towards what the island is short of (a target mix of jobs, plus a partner for a lonely bridge). A clear shape always keeps its job.
- Stats come from each model's own shape, so two polywogs with the same job still differ. All three change movement today: **Speed** (walking pace), **Bounce** (hop height, highest for ball shapes) and **Stamina** (how far it walks before resting).

## Also in this PR

- Polywogs push apart and bump instead of overlapping.
- Names are cleaned (letters, numbers and a few marks, 20 characters max) and only ever shown as plain text.
- A GitHub Pages workflow that runs the tests, builds and publishes the site from `main`.
- Unit tests (job scoring, island needs, stats, movement, bumping, names) and integration tests (real STL bytes through the import code). 39 in total: `npm test`.

## How to test

```
npm install
npm test
npm run dev
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:5195/island/ and drop in Tinkercad STLs. A cylinder and a sphere come out as keepers and a cone as a fan, each moving differently.

## Not in this PR

Job behaviours that follow the island-computer (couriers on the threads, keepers in rows, paired bridges) wait until those parts of the island exist.

pull_requests.title: Day 1: a kid's Tinkercad model comes alive on the island
pull_requests.author: jtbinith
pull_requests.description:
## What this does

A kid's Tinkercad model comes alive on the island.

1. Drop an STL exported from Tinkercad onto the island page (or use the "+ Add a Tinkercad model" button).
2. It drops from the sky and lands as a plain grey shape, like an unpainted Tinkercad part.
3. It shivers, its colour climbs from its feet to its head in blocky steps, it stretches and does a first excited hop.
4. Then it wanders the meadow, hopping as it walks and resting between walks. The grass parts around it.

Every model gets the same toy-toon look automatically: 3 hard light bands, a boiling ink outline and a candy colour from the look guide.

## How it works

- `web/look/creature.ts` reads the STL, turns Tinkercad's Z-up millimetres into an upright creature (20 mm = 1 unit tall, clamped to 0.5 to 2), keeps sharp edges sharp and smooths curves, and builds the toon material with the wake-up colour sweep.
- `web/island/creatures.ts` handles importing, landing on open ground near where the camera looks, the wake-up timeline, wandering and telling the grass where to part.
- `web/look/island.ts` makes the meadow grass lean away from up to 64 creatures.

## How to test

```
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:5195/island/, zoom in a little, and drop one or more `.stl` files from Tinkercad onto the page. Tested with Tinkercad's default cylinder, sphere and cone exports and a real kid-style model (about 24k triangles).

## Not in this PR

Sharing the world across devices, polywog jobs and the micro:bit come in later PRs.
